_meta.indication: Treatment of adult and pediatric patients with inhalational anthrax due to Bacillus anthracis in combination with appropriate antibacterial drugs, and for prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax when alternative therapies are not available or are not appropriate

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Cynomolgus macaque model study #724-G005829 (raxibacumab vs placebo)
pivotal_trials.phase: Animal efficacy study under the Animal Rule (21 CFR 601.90-95)
pivotal_trials.design: Placebo-controlled survival study in cynomolgus macaques challenged with aerosolized B. anthracis spores; treatment given when protective antigen (PA) was detected in blood
pivotal_trials.population: Cynomolgus macaques with systemic inhalational anthrax following aerosol spore challenge
pivotal_trials.result: 28-day survival 9/13 (69%) with 40 mg/kg raxibacumab vs 0/10 placebo; 95% CI for treatment difference (31.1, 88.9)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: NZW rabbit model study #682-G005758 (raxibacumab vs placebo)
pivotal_trials.phase: Animal efficacy study under the Animal Rule (21 CFR 601.90-95)
pivotal_trials.design: Placebo-controlled survival study in New Zealand White rabbits with inhalational anthrax; treatment given when rabbits had sustained fever or when PA was detected in blood
pivotal_trials.population: New Zealand White rabbits with inhalational anthrax following aerosol spore challenge
pivotal_trials.result: 14-day survival 6/17 (37%) with 40 mg/kg raxibacumab vs 0/13 placebo; 95% CI for treatment difference (7.3, 59.6)

key_safety: Safety studied only in healthy volunteers; most frequent adverse reactions were rash (2.8% total), pain in extremity (2.1%), pruritus (2.1%), and somnolence (1.5%). Infusion reactions (rash, urticaria, pruritus) may occur; premedicate with diphenhydramine. Four subjects (1.2%) discontinued infusion for adverse reactions.
target_moa: Monoclonal antibody that binds the protective antigen (PA) component of B. anthracis toxin, inhibiting PA binding to the anthrax toxin receptor on host cells; it has no direct antibacterial activity

advisory_committee.vote: Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee, November 2, 2012: voted YES 16, NO 1, ABSTAIN 1 that the therapeutic studies provide substantial evidence that raxibacumab is reasonably likely to produce clinical benefit; and YES 18, NO 0, ABSTAIN 0 on acceptable risk-benefit profile

description.text: Expanded indication to include pediatric patients with weight-based dosing for inhalational anthrax

citations.quote: Raxibacumab is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with inhalational anthrax due to *Bacillus anthracis* in combination with appropriate antibacterial drugs. Raxibacumab is also indicated for prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax when alternative therapies are not available or are not appropriate.

summary.text: Raxibacumab (BLA 125349) was approved for inhalational anthrax based solely on animal efficacy studies under the Animal Rule (21 CFR 601.90-95), as controlled human trials with intentional anthrax exposure are not ethical or feasible. The product received fast track designation (2003), orphan drug designation (2003), and priority review. The application was originally received May 14, 2009, received a Complete Response letter November 14, 2009, was resubmitted June 15, 2012, and approved December 14, 2012 following a positive Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee vote.

citations.quote: The effectiveness of raxibacumab is based solely on efficacy studies in animal models of inhalational anthrax. It is not ethical or feasible to conduct controlled clinical trials with intentional exposure of humans to anthrax. [see *Clinical Studies (14.1)*]
The applicant has submitted a synopsis for a future field study required for a BLA submitted pursuant to 21CFR§601.90-95.
The BLA was submitted May 14, 2009, given a priority review (the product has both fast-track designation and orphan designation), and scheduled for Advisory Committee meeting held October 27, 2009.

The Biologics License Application (BLA) 125,349 for raxibacumab was originally received on May 14, 2009 and a Complete Response letter was issued by the Agency on November 14, 2009. The application was resubmitted to the Agency on June 15, 2012 and was deemed a complete response to the deficiencies noted in the November 14, 2009 letter (see Section 2 of this review).
